title: Short: "A mountain taller than the world"

lines.text: There's a rule for how tall a mountain can get. On this asteroid, it says three hundred and forty kilometres.
The asteroid is Vesta, about five hundred kilometres across.
From its surface to its centre is only about two hundred and sixty kilometres.
So that mountain would be taller than the world beneath it.
What Vesta really has is a crater at its south pole, five hundred kilometres wide.
lines.cue: caption: SOUTH POLE CRATER: 500 KM WIDE

lines.text: Nearly as wide as Vesta itself, and nineteen kilometres deep.
Right in the middle, a peak about twenty kilometres high.
So where does the rule break? The full video on our channel explains the break. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
